fields.features_heading: The Working Parts of a Skin Type Quiz
fields.features_subheading: A prompt names the four types and what each result shows. Emergent builds the questions, the mapping, and the table behind them.
fields.feature_1:
Every option pointed at one type

Name the results you want, such as dry, oily, combination, and normal. Emergent builds the questions and the option-to-type mapping, and a later prompt rewords any question.
fields.feature_2:
A routine on every result screen

Give each type its own product list, and the result screen shows that routine the moment a taker finishes. Swap one product in a follow-up prompt and the next taker sees it.
fields.feature_3:
Answers saved beside the result

Each finished quiz lands as one row in a database you own: the type, every answer, and when it arrived. Filter the table by type before you plan a restock or a campaign.
fields.feature_4:
An email when a result lands

Choose the types that matter, and the app emails you each time one arrives, answers included. Point the alert at Slack instead so the counter team sees it between customers.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen, no caps

Takers answer one question per screen on a phone, with a progress bar running to the result. Emergent puts no cap on responses, and a launch week never cuts anyone off.
fields.feature_6:
A quiz that runs on your domain

Host the quiz on a domain of yours, included with Emergent and paid in credits. Paid plans export the full code to your GitHub repository for a developer to take it on.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Skin Type Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a skin type quiz that names each taker's type and saves every result with its answers.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the types the quiz can name
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask how a bare face feels
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Give the T-zone its own option
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Point every option at one type
fields.howto_step_1_des: Settle the four results first, because every option will point at one of them. Sensitive skin is not about how much or little oil skin produces, so ask about sensitivity as a separate flag rather than a fifth result.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Start with how a bare face feels an hour after washing, with nothing applied: tight, shiny, shiny only in spots, or comfortable. That one question separates the four types more cleanly than anything about products, which is why it belongs first.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Shine questions need an answer for the T-zone alone, because combination skin hides inside averages. A blotting test makes it concrete: 30 minutes after washing, press a blotting paper along the T-zone and the cheeks, and ask where it picked up oil.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Map each option to exactly one of the four types, and give the deciding questions, like the bare-face one, extra weight. Tell Emergent the mapping in plain English, and it builds the scoring where the type with the most points wins.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Write a routine for each result
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write the result screens before launch, one per type, each listing the products you would hand that person over the counter. A result that ends at a name sends the taker off to search; one that ends in a routine keeps them on your site.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Answer the quiz 4 times before launch, once as each type, and confirm the right result and routine come back. Then open the table and check all 4 rows landed with their answers, because those rows feed every follow-up you send.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Put it where skin questions start
fields.howto_step_7_des: Place the quiz on the pages where people already wonder about their skin: the homepage, a cleanser's product page, the signup flow. Read the first 50 rows, and when an answer pattern looks confused, reword that question with one prompt.

faq_plan.q: What is a skin type quiz?
faq_plan.a: A skin type quiz is a short run of questions about how skin feels bare and behaves through the day, ending in a named type. Dermatology usually classifies skin by five types: dry, oily, normal, combination, or sensitive. The quiz on this page asks 8 questions and sorts answers into the first four.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a skin type quiz?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI survey builder in one prompt: the types you want, the questions to ask, and what each result screen shows. Emergent builds the quiz and the logic behind it, and the app saves every finished quiz with its answers. Name any change in a later prompt, from a question's wording to the products on a result screen.

faq_plan.q: What should a skincare quiz ask before it recommends products?
faq_plan.a: Ask how skin feels an hour after washing, where shine shows by midday, how pores look, and how a new cream sits after a week. Add one question on scent if you carry fragrance-free lines, and keep the whole skincare quiz under 10 questions so people finish it at a counter or on a bus.

faq_plan.q: Is a Fitzpatrick skin type quiz the same as the one on this page?
faq_plan.a: No. The Fitzpatrick skin type is a classification first developed in 1975 by Thomas Fitzpatrick, MD, with six phototypes going from light to dark. The quiz here sorts by oil and comfort instead, the way a style quiz sorts by taste, and its takers land on a routine rather than a phototype.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a find your skin type quiz ask?
faq_plan.a: Six to 10, if each question separates at least two types. One bare-face question, a midday shine check, pores, a season change, and a blotting test cover the ground without losing anyone. Emergent sets no response caps, and a short quiz can sit on every page of your site at once.

faq_plan.q: What is a Baumann skin type quiz based on?
faq_plan.a: The Baumann system is composed of 4 spectra, starting with dry to oily and sensitive to resistant, which cross into 16 skin types. Build on it only if you can write 16 distinct result screens; a four-type quiz keeps every result backed by products you carry.

faq_plan.q: How is a skin type quiz different from seeing a dermatologist?
faq_plan.a: A skin type quiz reads what a person reports; a dermatologist examines the skin itself. Skin type can also change over the course of a life; treat any result as a snapshot. Keep result copy descriptive rather than clinical: a quiz can place someone the way a vocabulary quiz places a reading level, and it should never diagnose.

faq_plan.q: Can I run a skin type quiz for free?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing. Paid plans add full code export to a GitHub repository you own, which matters once a developer takes the quiz over.

faq_plan.q: How does a skin types quiz tell combination from normal?
faq_plan.a: By where the shine sits. A T-zone that turns shiny by midday while the cheeks stay comfortable points to combination; no shine and no tightness anywhere points to normal. In a matching quiz each option adds a point to one type; write the shine options so the two types never blur.

faq_plan.q: What should the result screen of a what's my skin type quiz offer next?
faq_plan.a: Give the taker somewhere to go: the routine for that type, a link to each product in it, and one opt-in for a follow-up email. A sample offer or a free trial landing page converts takers who want proof before a full-size purchase. The app stores each result beside its answers, and the follow-up can quote exactly what someone said.

quiz.title: What Is Your Skin Type?
quiz.intro: Eight questions about how your bare skin feels and behaves. The result names the type your answers lean toward, a starting point for a routine, not a medical finding.

questions.explanation: This mirrors the paper test dermatology sources describe: after 30 minutes, gently press a blotting paper on your skin, blotting along the T-zone and cheeks.

source.quote: After 30 minutes, gently press a blotting paper on your skin, making sure to blot along your T-zone and cheeks

results.title: Dry
results.description: Your answers lean dry: tightness after washing, little midday shine, and flaking when the weather turns. Favor a non-foaming cleanser and a richer moisturizer morning and night, and give any new product a full week on skin before judging it.

results.title: Oily
results.description: Your answers lean oily: shine that returns by midday and products that slide. Reach for a gel moisturizer and a foaming cleanser first, keep layers light, and judge each product after a week on skin rather than a day.

results.title: Combination
results.description: Your answers lean combination: a T-zone that shines while the cheeks stay comfortable or even tight. Treat the two zones separately, a lighter layer down the center and a richer one on the cheeks, instead of averaging one product across both.

results.title: Normal
results.description: Your answers lean normal: comfortable after washing, little shine, few surprises between seasons. Keep the routine short, a cleanser, a moisturizer, and sunscreen, and change one product at a time so you can tell what helped.

Every result is saved with its answers in a database the owner keeps. The FAQ separates this quiz from the Fitzpatrick and Baumann systems and from a dermatologist's visit.
